_no_test_command: There is none, and that absence is the point. This module is judged entirely by the language-neutral cases in conformance.json, driven over the wire, so nothing about how it is verified mentions JavaScript. That is what makes the slot fillable by another language.
_artifact_side: This file is hashed into the ARTIFACT, not the contract. Change the image and this implementation is re-judged; but the Python implementation of the same interface fills the SAME contract slot rather than inventing a new one.
_pinned_by_digest: A tag is a moving target: `node:20-alpine` meant different bytes last month and will mean different bytes next month. Since this file is hashed into the ARTIFACT, a tag meant two different runtimes could share one artifact digest — the exact defect that disqualified Extism. The digest makes 'it passed' a claim about a runtime that can be produced again.
